Prove that SHADERed's current debugger core can run in a Worker and reproduce a bounded subset of Shadergrove fragment shaders.

## Priority and scope

Recommended priority: **P0**. Workstream: **Debugger**.

## Dependencies

- https://github.com/antelm-dev/shadergrove/issues/52

## Implementation scope

- Port and pin SPIRV-VM with the minimum C/WASM wrapper for program creation, inputs, stepping, variable inspection and cleanup.
- Compile debug SPIR-V with names/line information and an explicit supported-opcode/capability policy.
- Exercise arithmetic, control flow, functions, uniforms, textures, discard and derivative cases; document unsupported features.
- Apply instruction/time/memory limits and cancellation to shader execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A reproducible WASM build and browser/Electron loading proof are recorded.
- [ ] For the supported subset, VM output matches WebGL reference pixels within documented tolerances.
- [ ] Texture filtering, derivatives and precision limitations are explicitly tested or rejected.
- [ ] Malformed/unsupported programs and runaway execution return actionable errors and allow Worker recovery.
- [ ] Produce a go/no-go conclusion before committing the product to full debugger support.

## Deferred work

Compute, geometry/tessellation, all SPIR-V opcodes and claims of exact GPU execution.

## Upstream references

- https://github.com/dfranx/SPIRV-VM
- https://github.com/dfranx/SPIRV-VM/blob/439434fce991ea9c5e9c1b78ebcbcb22bb27feaf/OPCODES.txt
- https://github.com/dfranx/SHADERed/tree/780e96791fd8ac48f1f656309211660d78ff9095/src/SHADERed/Objects/DebugInformation.cpp

## Current integration points

- apps/studio/src/app/rendering/shader-engine.ts

Baseline: Shadergrove develop at de631ea. Refresh contracts and validate the current checkout before implementation. This issue tracks planned work; source inspection is not proof of porting or runtime compatibility.
title: Validate a WebAssembly port of SPIRV-VM for fragment shader debugging

## Goal

Create a shared analysis service for GLSL ES projects, supplying semantic editor data and debug compilation without blocking the UI.

## Priority and scope

Recommended priority: **P0**. Workstream: **Language tooling**.

## Dependencies

No prerequisite issue in this initiative.

## Implementation scope

- Define typed requests/results with project revision, document/pass IDs, capabilities and diagnostics.
- Reuse Shadergrove Common/include composition and source spans, including renderer-generated prefixes and uniforms.
- Evaluate glslang for validation/AST analysis and SPIR-V generation; keep actual WebGL driver diagnostics authoritative for rendering.
- Separate ESSL validation from the normalization required for debug SPIR-V; preserve source locations.
- Audit and pin upstream components and licenses; preserve required copyright/notices for redistributed code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Analysis runs in a Worker with cancellation, bounded work and rejection of stale results.
- [ ] Diagnostics from Common, includes and generated wrappers reveal the correct original document/line.
- [ ] Supported GLSL ES versions and WebGL/SPIR-V differences are documented and exercised with representative shaders.
- [ ] Record reproducible dependency versions, licensing and browser/Electron packaging requirements.

## Deferred work

Full language server protocol, additional shader languages and changing the rendering backend.

## Upstream references

- https://github.com/dfranx/SHADERed/tree/780e96791fd8ac48f1f656309211660d78ff9095/src/SHADERed/Objects/ShaderCompiler.cpp
- https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang

## Current integration points

- libs/shared/src/project/pass-source.ts
- apps/studio/src/app/editor/monaco-loader.ts
- apps/studio/src/app/rendering/engine/pass-compiler.ts

Baseline: Shadergrove develop at de631ea. Refresh contracts and validate the current checkout before implementation. This issue tracks planned work; source inspection is not proof of porting or runtime compatibility.

## Goal

Provide an optional assistant directly inside Shader Studio while keeping the product independent from any single model provider.

## Scope

- Add a provider abstraction with initial OpenAI and Anthropic adapters.
- Support bring-your-own API key and leave room for future Shader Studio-managed billing/credits.
- Store credentials only server-side or in the desktop OS credential store; never expose them to browser bundles, logs, exports, or project files.
- Build a chat/command panel aware of the active project, selected documents, diagnostics, controls, and current render.
- Route model actions through the same typed operations used by MCP.
- Present proposed edits as reviewable diffs; compile and render previews before allowing save.
- Add cancellation, streaming, usage/cost visibility, provider/model selection, and conversation reset.
- Document data sent to each provider and provide per-request context controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- Users can configure either OpenAI or Anthropic without changing application code.
- The assistant can propose a patch, compile it, explain diagnostics, and show a preview without automatically saving.
- No provider credential reaches client-visible state or telemetry.
- Provider errors, limits, cancellation, and unavailable models are handled consistently.
- Users can inspect which project data will be sent before the first request.
- Core orchestration is covered by provider-independent tests with mocked adapters.

## Product wording

Use **Connect Shader Studio to ChatGPT/Claude** for external connectors. Use **Configure an AI provider** for this embedded assistant; a consumer ChatGPT/Claude subscription must not be presented as API access.
title: Add a provider-agnostic AI assistant inside Shader Studio

## Goal

Make Shader Studio installable and discoverable in ChatGPT/Codex as a native plugin backed by the remote MCP server.

## Depends on

- #12 — authenticated remote MCP endpoint.

## Scope

- Package the existing MCP capabilities as an OpenAI-compatible plugin.
- Add plugin metadata, skills/instructions, authentication configuration, icons, privacy links, and support information.
- Add an optional compact UI card for shader/project state and render previews where it materially improves the workflow.
- Optimize tool metadata and permissions for discovery, approval, and safe mutation.
- Add a **Connect to ChatGPT** entry point in Shader Studio.
- Test in developer mode, address submission requirements, and prepare marketplace/publication assets.

## Acceptance criteria

- The plugin installs successfully in a clean ChatGPT/Codex environment.
- Users can list/open a shader, patch GLSL, compile, inspect diagnostics, tune parameters, and view a render.
- Draft changes are clearly distinguished from persisted saves.
- Destructive tools use explicit approval semantics.
- OAuth disconnect/revocation prevents subsequent access.
- Submission validation passes and the publication checklist is documented.
title: Package and publish a ChatGPT plugin for Shader Studio

## Goal

Let users add Shader Studio to Claude as a custom connector and operate their shader workspace conversationally.

## Depends on

- #12 — authenticated remote MCP endpoint.

## Scope

- Validate the remote MCP endpoint and OAuth flow with Claude web/Desktop custom connectors.
- Add a **Connect to Claude** flow in Shader Studio with concise setup instructions and connection status.
- Optimize tool names, descriptions, instructions, and deferred loading for Claude tool selection.
- Define safe default permissions and approval behavior for read, draft mutation, save, revert, and delete operations.
- Provide example workflows: inspect a project, patch GLSL, compile, diagnose, tune parameters, render variants, and save after approval.
- Add connector-specific troubleshooting and privacy documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can authenticate Shader Studio from Claude and enable it in a conversation.
- Claude can complete the read → patch → compile → render loop without manual data copying.
- Saving, reverting, and deleting require an explicit user-visible confirmation policy.
- Screenshots/renders are returned in a form Claude can display.
- Disconnecting the connector revokes further access.
- A documented end-to-end smoke test is repeatable on a clean account.
title: Add first-class Claude connector onboarding

## Goal

Make Shader Studio callable from cloud-hosted AI clients by adding a production-ready remote MCP transport alongside the existing local stdio bridge.

## Scope

- Expose a stable HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.
- Reuse the existing MCP tool/resource definitions rather than maintaining a second contract.
- Add OAuth 2.1-compatible authorization, token refresh/revocation, and per-user/per-workspace isolation.
- Define the routing model for cloud-hosted Shader Studio and local/desktop instances connected through an outbound relay or tunnel.
- Add tool-level scopes and preserve MCP read-only/destructive/idempotent annotations.
- Add rate limiting, audit events, request size/time limits, origin/host validation, and safe error mapping.
- Document deployment, self-hosting, privacy, and data-retention implications.

## Acceptance criteria

- A standards-compliant remote MCP client can initialize, list tools, and invoke an authorized read-only tool over HTTPS.
- Anonymous, expired, cross-user, and cross-workspace requests are rejected.
- Mutating tools cannot operate outside the authorized workspace/session.
- Local stdio usage remains backward compatible.
- Integration tests cover authentication, isolation, reconnect/stream behavior, and revocation.
- A threat model and deployment runbook are included.

## Architectural decision required

Choose and document one supported first release path:

1. Cloud-hosted Shader Studio workspaces, or
2. An outbound desktop/self-hosted relay that does not expose localhost directly.
title: Expose an authenticated remote MCP endpoint over Streamable HTTP

## Goal

Replace the current manual MCP setup and `localStorage` token pairing flow with a first-class **AI integrations** experience inside Shader Studio.

## Scope

- Add an **AI integrations** screen accessible from the application settings/menu.
- Present guided setup for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and generic MCP clients.
- Generate, rotate, copy, and revoke the local pairing token without using browser developer tools.
- Show connection state, connected client, last activity, protocol/version compatibility, and actionable errors.
- Keep the existing loopback-only and single-tab security guarantees.
- Cover web and Electron behavior, including Windows-specific `npx` guidance where still required.
- Update English/French translations and MCP documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can pair a supported local MCP client without opening developer tools or editing `localStorage`.
- Secrets are never logged or persisted in source-controlled configuration.
- The UI distinguishes disconnected, waiting, connected, incompatible, and error states.
- Token rotation immediately invalidates the previous pairing.
- Existing CLI/environment-variable setup remains supported.
- Automated tests cover token lifecycle and connection-state presentation.
title: Add an AI integrations screen for local MCP pairing
